questions.question: The population of a village is increased by 3%. Had there been 122 less, there would have been a decrease of 1%. Find the original population.

⇒ 0.04P = 122

⇒ P = 122 / 0.04

⇒ P = 3050

**∴ The original population of the village is 3050.**

questions.question: Eight persons went to a restaurant for lunch. Seven of them spent ₹80 each on their meals, while the eighth person spent ₹70 more than the average expenditure of all eight persons. What was the total amount spent by all the individuals?

Average expenditure = Total expenditure / Number of persons

Let the amount spent by the 8th person be x.

Average expenditure = T / 8

T = (7 × 80) + x

⇒ T = 720

**∴ The total amount spent by all the individuals is ₹720.**

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India states that the Parliament consists of the President of India and the two Houses of Parliament known as Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and House of the People (Lok Sabha)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 79**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 79** of the Constitution of India states that the Parliament consists of the President of India and the two Houses of Parliament, namely the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
 
• The President of India is an integral part of the Parliament, although not a member of either House.
 
• The Parliament operates as a bicameral legislature with **Rajya Sabha representing the states and union territories** and **Lok Sabha representing the citizens** through direct elections.
 
• This article is a fundamental provision under **Part V (The Union) and Chapter II (Parliament)** of the Constitution of India.
 
• Article 79 establishes the structure and functioning of the Parliament, ensuring a collaborative legislative process between the President and the two Houses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajya Sabha (Council of States)**

 
 
• Rajya Sabha is the upper house of Parliament, representing the states and union territories of India.
 
• It is a **permanent body** that is not subject to dissolution, with one-third of its members retiring every two years.
 
• The **maximum strength** of Rajya Sabha is capped at 250 members as per Article 80 of the Constitution.
 
• The Vice President of India acts as the **ex-officio Chairman** of Rajya Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Lok Sabha (House of the People)**
 
 
• Lok Sabha is the lower house of Parliament, with members directly elected by the citizens of India.
 
• The maximum strength of Lok Sabha is **552 members**, including up to 20 members representing Union Territories.
 
• The Speaker of Lok Sabha presides over its sessions and ensures the orderly conduct of business.
 
• It serves as the principal legislative body for **enacting laws** and addressing the needs of the electorate.
 
 
 
• **Role of the President in Parliament**
 
 
• The President summons and prorogues sessions of Parliament and grants assent to bills to convert them into laws.
 
• The President can **dissolve Lok Sabha** and call for fresh elections when necessary.
 
• Under Article 123, the President can issue ordinances when Parliament is not in session.
 
• The President is a crucial part of the legislative process but does not vote or participate in debates.
 
 
 
• **Bicameral Legislature System**
 
 
• India follows a bicameral legislature, consisting of two houses: Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha.
 
• The system ensures **checks and balances** in the legislative process, preventing hasty decisions.
 
• Rajya Sabha focuses on states and union territories, while Lok Sabha represents citizens directly.
 
• Countries like the USA, UK, and Canada also follow bicameral legislature systems.

questions.question: Which of the following was the capital of the Pallava Dynasty?

__
 
• **Kanchipuram** served as the capital of the Pallava Dynasty, which ruled parts of South India from the 3rd to 9th centuries CE.
 
• The Pallavas are renowned for their contributions to **Dravidian art and architecture**, and Kanchipuram became a prominent center for temple architecture under their reign.
 
• The city is home to notable structures such as the **Kailasanatha Temple** and **Vaikunta Perumal Temple**, exemplifying the architectural advancements during the Pallava era.
 
• Kanchipuram was also an important center for **learning and spirituality**, fostering both Hinduism and Buddhism during the Pallava period.
 
• The Pallavas played a key role in spreading Indian art, architecture, and culture to Southeast Asia through trade and cultural exchanges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pallava Dynasty**

 
 
• The Pallavas were a powerful South Indian dynasty that ruled over Tamil Nadu and parts of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• They were contemporaries of other prominent dynasties like the Chalukyas and Pandyas.
 
• Their reign marked the transition from **rock-cut architecture to structural temples**, influencing later dynasties such as the Cholas.
 
• They were patrons of both **Sanskrit and Tamil literature**, contributing significantly to the cultural and intellectual heritage of South India.
 
 
 
• **Kanchipuram**
 
 
• Known as the **"City of Thousand Temples"**, Kanchipuram is one of the seven sacred cities of Hinduism.
 
• It served as a major political, economic, and spiritual hub during the Pallava period.
 
• The city is famous for **Kanchipuram silk sarees**, which are a significant cultural legacy.
 
• It has been a center for various religious traditions, including Shaivism, Vaishnavism, and Jainism.
 
 
 
• **Pallava Architecture**
 
 
• The Pallavas pioneered **rock-cut architecture**, evident in the Mahabalipuram cave temples.
 
• Later, they transitioned to structural temples made of stone, such as the **Kailasanatha Temple** in Kanchipuram.
 
• The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram, built during Pallava rule, is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
 
• Their architectural innovations set the foundation for Dravidian temple architecture in South India.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance**
 
 
• The Pallavas were instrumental in spreading Indian culture and religion to Southeast Asia through maritime trade and cultural exchanges.
 
• Their inscriptions, written in both Tamil and Sanskrit, provide valuable insights into the political and cultural history of ancient South India.
 
• Their governance and cultural achievements laid the groundwork for subsequent South Indian dynasties, such as the Cholas.
 
• Their advancements in art and architecture had a lasting impact on the cultural landscape of India and beyond.

• **Kamalini Asthana** is a renowned exponent of the classical Indian dance form Kathak.
 
• Kathak is one of the eight recognized classical dance forms of India, known for its intricate footwork, spins, and storytelling through expressions.

• Kathak has three prominent gharanas (schools): Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula for potassium permanganate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**KMnO₄**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Potassium permanganate has the chemical formula **KMnO₄**, consisting of potassium (K), manganese (Mn), and oxygen (O).
 
• It is a dark purple crystalline compound widely used as a **strong oxidizing agent** in chemical reactions.
 
• KMnO₄ readily dissolves in water to form potassium ions (K⁺) and permanganate ions (MnO₄−).
 
• The manganese in KMnO₄ has an oxidation state of **+7**, which contributes to its oxidizing properties.
 
• Potassium permanganate is used in **water treatment, disinfection, and various oxidation reactions in organic and inorganic chemistry.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxidizing Properties of KMnO₄:**

 
 
• In acidic conditions, KMnO₄ reduces to Mn²⁺, releasing oxygen and acting as a strong oxidizer.
 
• In neutral or alkaline mediums, it reduces to MnO₂ (manganese dioxide).
 
• Its oxidizing ability is useful in redox titrations and industrial applications.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Potassium Permanganate:**
 
 
• It is used for **purifying and disinfecting water** by oxidizing organic impurities and iron or manganese in water.
 
• Medicinally, it is employed as an antiseptic for treating skin conditions like fungal infections and wounds.
 
• In organic chemistry, KMnO₄ is used to oxidize alkenes to glycols and alcohols to carboxylic acids.
 
 
 
• **Structure of Permanganate Ion:**
 
 
• The permanganate ion (MnO₄−) has a tetrahedral geometry.
 
• Manganese is surrounded by four oxygen atoms, with double-bond character distributed via resonance.
 
 
 
• **Safety Considerations:**
 
 
• KMnO₄ is a strong oxidizer and can ignite combustible materials upon contact.
 
• Direct contact can cause skin irritation and permanent stains, while ingestion is toxic and harmful.
 
• It should be stored in a cool, dry place, away from organic materials to prevent decomposition.

Statements:

A. They include horsetails and ferns.

B. Pteridophytes are used for medicinal purposes and as soil-binders.

D. Evolutionarily, they are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues – xylem and phloem.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only A, B and D**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pteridophytes** include horsetails and ferns, which are vascular plants widely distributed in terrestrial ecosystems. (Source: NCERT Biology Textbook, Class 11)
 
• Pteridophytes serve ecological and economic purposes, such as being used for medicinal applications and acting as soil-binders to prevent erosion. (Source: Current Environmental Science Research)
 
• Evolutionarily, pteridophytes are the **first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues** like xylem and phloem for water and nutrient transportation. (Source: NCERT Biology Textbook, Class 11)
 
• Pteridophytes are ancient plants that bridge the gap between bryophytes and gymnosperms; they are not recently evolved or highly advanced plants. (Source: Evolutionary Botany Studies)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vascular Tissues in Plants:**

 
 
• Xylem primarily carries water and dissolved minerals, while phloem transports organic nutrients like sugars.
 
• The presence of vascular tissues marks the evolutionary advancement of pteridophytes compared to bryophytes.
 
 
 
• **Horsetails and Ferns:**
 
 
• Horsetails belong to the genus *Equisetum* and are characterized by jointed stems and spore-based reproduction.
 
• Ferns are non-flowering vascular plants with large, divided leaves known as fronds.
 
• Both horsetails and ferns are widely used in horticulture and ecological restoration projects.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Role of Pteridophytes:**
 
 
• Pteridophytes contribute to soil stabilization, especially in areas prone to erosion.
 
• They play an important role in the carbon cycle by sequestering carbon dioxide through photosynthesis.
 
• Several species are utilized for ornamental purposes due to their aesthetic foliage.
 
 
 
• **Evolutionary Importance:**
 
 
• Pteridophytes bridge the evolutionary gap between non-vascular bryophytes and seed-bearing gymnosperms.
 
• They exhibit structural adaptations such as true roots, stems, and leaves, reflecting significant evolutionary progress.
 
• Unlike bryophytes, they reproduce via spores and do not depend on water for fertilization.

questions.question: By which of the following Amendments was the right to property removed from Part III of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**44th Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **44th Amendment Act** of the Indian Constitution, enacted in **1978**, removed the right to property from the category of Fundamental Rights under Part III of the Constitution.
 
• After the amendment, the right to property was reclassified as a **legal right** under Article 300A in Part XII of the Constitution.
 
• This change was made during the tenure of the **Janata Party government**, led by Prime Minister **Morarji Desai**.
 
• The primary objective of this amendment was to facilitate **land reforms** and prevent misuse of the right to property by affluent individuals to challenge government policies.
 
• Post-amendment, property disputes are dealt with as violations of legal rights rather than Fundamental Rights, ensuring streamlined governance and justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights in Part III**

 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Articles 12 to 35 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These rights are essential for safeguarding individual freedoms and are enforceable by the courts.
 
• Major Fundamental Rights include the Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
 
 
• **Legal Rights vs Fundamental Rights**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights are protected by the Constitution and cannot be altered without constitutional amendment.
 
• Legal rights are granted by ordinary legislation and can be modified or revoked by the legislature.
 
• The 44th Amendment reclassified the right to property as a legal right under Article 300A.
 
 
 
• **Article 300A of the Constitution**
 
 
• Article 300A states: "No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law."
 
• This provision ensures that property can only be taken by the government through legally established procedures.
 
 
 
• **Land Reforms in India**
 
 
• Land reforms aim to redistribute land ownership and increase agricultural productivity.
 
• The removal of the right to property as a Fundamental Right facilitated initiatives like the abolition of the zamindari system and ceilings on landholding.

questions.question: Divergent plate boundary is a boundary that occurs between two tectonic plates:

options.text: that are moving towards one another
where one plate slides beneath the other
that are sliding horizontally past each other
that are moving away from one another

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Divergent plate boundary is a boundary that occurs between two tectonic plates that are moving away from one another.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Divergent plate boundaries occur where two tectonic plates move away from each other, creating a gap.
 
• These boundaries are often associated with the formation of new oceanic crust as magma rises from the mantle to fill the gap.
 
• Shallow earthquakes and volcanic activity are common phenomena observed at divergent boundaries.
 
• Examples of divergent boundaries include mid-ocean ridges like the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
 
• The process of seafloor spreading is a hallmark of divergent plate boundaries, contributing to the gradual expansion of ocean basins.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tectonic Plate Boundaries**

 
 
• The Earth's lithosphere is divided into tectonic plates that move relative to each other.
 
• There are three main types of plate boundaries: divergent (moving apart), convergent (moving together), and transform (sliding past one another).
 
• These boundaries are responsible for geological phenomena such as earthquakes, volcanic activity, and mountain formation.
 
 
 
• **Seafloor Spreading**
 
 
• Occurs at divergent plate boundaries where magma rises and solidifies to create new crust.
 
• Magnetic anomalies on the ocean floor provide evidence for this process, showing symmetrical patterns on either side of mid-ocean ridges.
 
 
 
• **Mid-Ocean Ridges**
 
 
• Underwater mountain ranges formed by divergent plate boundaries.
 
• Known for high volcanic activity and the generation of new crust.
 
• Examples include the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and the East Pacific Rise.
 
 
 
• **Rift Zones**
 
 
• Occur when divergent boundaries form within continental plates, creating rift valleys.
 
• Over time, these rift zones can evolve into ocean basins.
 
• The East African Rift is a prominent example of an active rift zone.

questions.question: Who discovered the Bharhut stupa?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alexander Cunningham**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Alexander Cunningham**, regarded as the "Father of Indian Archaeology," discovered the Bharhut Stupa in **1873**.
 
• He extensively documented the stupa's remains, including its intricate sculptures and inscriptions, which are valuable for understanding early Buddhist art and architecture.
 
• The Bharhut Stupa, located in present-day **Madhya Pradesh**, dates back to the **2nd century BCE**, showcasing early Buddhist relief carvings and inscriptions in the Brahmi script.
 
• Cunningham's discovery provided critical insights into the cultural and religious practices of the **Mauryan and Sunga periods**.
 
• His findings on Bharhut are recorded in his archaeological reports, which remain foundational for the study of ancient Indian history and early Buddhist art.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharhut Stupa**

 
 
• The Bharhut Stupa is an ancient Buddhist monument known for its remarkable railings and gateways adorned with narrative relief sculptures.
 
• Its carvings depict **Jataka tales** (stories of the Buddha’s previous lives) and other Buddhist symbols.
 
• It was originally commissioned during the **Mauryan Empire** and later renovated during the **Sunga dynasty**.
 
• Many artifacts from Bharhut, including reliefs and inscriptions, are now preserved in the **Indian Museum in Kolkata**.
 
 
 
• **Alexander Cunningham**
 
 
• Alexander Cunningham was the first **Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**, founded in 1861.
 
• He conducted pioneering archaeological explorations of major sites like **Sarnath, Taxila, and Bodh Gaya**.
 
• His systematic documentation and study of inscriptions helped reconstruct India’s ancient history and timeline.
 
• Cunningham's work laid the foundation for modern archaeology in India.
 
 
 
• **Buddhist Art and Architecture**
 
 
• The Bharhut Stupa is an example of **early Buddhist art**, characterized by narrative reliefs and symbolic depictions of Buddhist themes.
 
• Unlike later Buddhist monuments, early art like Bharhut avoided anthropomorphic representations of the Buddha, instead using symbols like the **lotus and wheel**.
 
• The railings and gateways of Bharhut illustrate the transition to more elaborate decorative elements seen in later sites like **Sanchi**.
 
• Inscriptions at Bharhut provide valuable evidence of early Buddhist practices, patronage, and the use of the **Brahmi script**.
 
 
 
• **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**
 
 
• The ASI, established in 1861, is responsible for preserving and documenting India’s cultural heritage.
 
• It conducts excavations, research, and conservation of historical monuments and archaeological sites.
 
• Under Cunningham’s leadership, the ASI began systematic archaeological surveys and excavations in India.
 
• The efforts of the ASI have been instrumental in understanding India’s ancient civilization and its contributions to global heritage.
